text:
Alice: FYI billing alert hit overnight — +$6.2k. Looks like europe-west1 GPU zone spiked in usage. Anyone seen weird autoscaler activity?
Ben: saw the alert at 07:15. digging into autoscaler logs now :eyes:
Ben: quick note — aws/gcp autoscaler shows a big scale event around 02:12 UTC, ~48 nodes launched for gpu-workers-pool. weird thing: the launch template seems to reference a CPU machine type. investigating.
infra-sre: can you paste `kubectl get nodes` and a gcloud compute list for europe-west1?
Ben: here's a quick snapshot:```bash
$ kubectl get nodes | grep gpu | wc -l
72
$ gcloud compute instances list --filter="zone:(europe-west1-*)" --format="table(name,machineType,status)" | grep gpu
gpu-worker-01    zones/europe-west1-b/machineTypes/n2-standard-32    RUNNING
gpu-worker-02    zones/europe-west1-c/machineTypes/n2-standard-32    RUNNING
gpu-worker-03    zones/europe-west1-b/machineTypes/n2-standard-32    RUNNING
... (many similar lines)
```
Alice: those are CPU VMs — that explains the mismatch. If the autoscaler used a non-GPU launch config, it still scaled pods but they landed on non-GPU machines (no GPU SKU billed?) Wait, finance — how does committed GPU reservation interact with this?
finance-bot: Quick billing summary: GPU reservations apply only to GPU SKUs. CPU-only instances do not consume GPU reservation credits. Preliminary estimate: ~ $5.8k of unreserved spend from those instances last night. Filing a billing dispute ticket with cloud support now.
Diana: where did the bad launch config come from? any recent infra changes?
Carl: I pushed a terraform change last week to add a fallback autoscaler template in case the GPU pool exhausted quota. I accidentally set `var.fallback_machine_type = "n2-standard-32"` in the module instead of the intended `a2-highgpu-1-preemptible`. The autoscaler policy prefers the fallback when node provisioning slows; it kicked in and started provisioning CPU nodes en masse.
Alice: ugh. So autoscaler fallback + missing accelerator constraint = mass CPU launches. Actions needed: 1) scale down the mis-provisioned pool 2) cordon/drain non-GPU nodes 3) fix terraform var + redeploy 4) open billing dispute + tag costs 5) add CI/guardrails to prevent future.
infra-sre: executing step 1 & 2 now.```bash
# cap the managed instance group to 0 to stop further launches
gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaled --region europe-west1\
  gpu-workers-mig --max-num-replicas=0 || true
# drain nodes without GPU taint
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | grep -v "gpu"); do kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force || true; done
```
infra-sre: scale-down started, ~48 non-GPU nodes are being deleted. added temporary autoscaler max cap=10 to limit blast radius and prevent additional fallbacks. Also patched node template to require accelerator-type label.
Ben: added quick helm guard in the node-provisioner values — assert `nodeSelector: accelerator: nvidia-tesla-t4` and a startup check that fails provisioning if accelerator missing. Will follow up with a proper admission webhook.
Carl: pushing terraform fix now — changing var and running `terraform plan`. PR opened: infra#384. Sorry team, my bad.
Alice: good. @Carl after merge please run `terraform apply` and confirm cluster templates. @Ben add CI check for launch config vs node taints. @Diana coordinate cost reconciliation with finance-bot and tag the spike to the right cost centers. I'll file an ops-incident for RCA and follow-up actions.
deploy-bot: Deployment 2025-11-12T03:45Z — Rollback of cluster-autoscaler fallback config by Carl (pr/384) — status: success :white_check_mark:
finance-bot: Billing ticket opened with cloud provider (case 987654). Asking for provisional credit while we complete RCA.
Alice: Postmortem owners: Alice (lead), Carl (config fix), Ben (prevention), Diana (cost reconciliation). Estimated follow-ups: billing dispute, CI webhook, add autoscaler acceptance test. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Ben: noted. adding acceptance test to infra pipeline this afternoon. :hammer_and_wrench:
